expected.form: J(0) = -b*I + P (P = cyclic permutation); eigenvalues are -b + cube roots of unity

independent_reference.source: Thomas, R. (1999), 'Deterministic chaos seen in terms of feedback circuits', Int. J. Bifurcation Chaos 9 (10), 1889-1905, defines the field; canonical b = 0.208186 per the Sprott 2003 catalog usage. The eigenvalue closed form follows from J(0) = -b*I + P with P the cyclic permutation matrix whose eigenvalues are the cube roots of unity (hand derivation in the derivation .md section 1); SymPy eigenvals (generator) and numpy.linalg.eigvals (sim test) agree.
independent_reference.derived_by: hand cube-roots-of-unity argument; SymPy eigenvals; numpy.linalg.eigvals cross-check

expected.form: on the symmetry diagonal x = y = z the field reduces to sin(u) = b*u: u = 0 and u = ±u* in (pi/2, pi)

independent_reference.source: Restriction of the field to the invariant diagonal (hand derivation in the derivation .md section 2). The transcendental root is anchored by three independent numerical routes: mpmath.findroot at 30 dps (generator), the sim reference's bisection, and the field-residual assertion in the sim test.
independent_reference.derived_by: hand diagonal reduction; mpmath 30-dps root; bisection + residual cross-check

expected.symmetry_form: f(Cx) = C f(x) exactly, C = cyclic rotation (x,y,z)->(y,z,x)

independent_reference.source: Trace of the hand-derived Jacobian (three -b diagonal entries; derivation .md section 3); the cyclic equivariance is direct substitution. SymPy verifies both symbolically (generator); the sim PBT invariants sample both numerically.
independent_reference.derived_by: hand trace + substitution; SymPy symbolic; PBT numerical sampling
